hull.definition: The main outer body of a submarine or ship.

conning-tower.definition: A raised submarine structure associated historically with command or observation; its arrangement depends on vessel design.

periscope.definition: An optical instrument that provides a view of an otherwise obstructed field.
periscope.exampleUsage: The museum guide showed how the periscope provided a view from a sheltered position.

hatch.definition: A door or opening in a vehicle, ship, or spacecraft.

porthole.definition: A window in a ship or airplane.

ballast-tank.definition: A tank filled with water or air to control a submarine's buoyancy.

propeller.definition: A mechanical device that rotates to push against air or water.
propeller.exampleUsage: The propeller rotated to produce thrust.

rudder.definition: A movable surface used to help steer a vessel through water.

torpedo-tube.definition: A tube used to launch torpedoes from a vessel; the lesson identifies the equipment without teaching its operation.

sonar-dome.definition: A rounded cover protecting sonar equipment.

control-panel.definition: A flat section of a device holds the buttons, switches, and dials that control its operation.
control-panel.exampleUsage: The control panel contained the system’s switches and controls.

navigation-screen.definition: An electronic display that shows information used to determine and monitor a vessel's position and route.
navigation-screen.exampleUsage: The navigation screen showed the submarine's planned route.

depth-gauge.definition: An instrument that shows how far below the water surface a vessel or object is.
depth-gauge.exampleUsage: The depth gauge showed that the submarine was descending.

compass.definition: A navigation instrument that indicates direction relative to a reference such as magnetic north.

radar.definition: A system that uses radio waves to detect objects or weather.

sonar-display.definition: A screen that presents information collected by sonar equipment using sound waves underwater.
sonar-display.exampleUsage: The sonar display showed echoes from objects ahead.

helm.definition: The controls used to steer a vessel.

throttle.definition: A control that adjusts an engine’s power or speed within its operating system.

communication-radio.definition: A radio system used for sending and receiving voice or data messages.
communication-radio.exampleUsage: The communication radio was tested before departure.

alarm.definition: A warning signal or device that alerts the crew to a problem.

bunk-bed.definition: A pair of beds is arranged vertically, with one bed positioned above the other.

galley.definition: The kitchen on a ship or submarine.

mess-hall.definition: A large shared dining facility where members of an organized group eat meals together, especially in military or residential settings.

storage-locker.definition: A small secured cupboard or compartment used to store equipment or personal items.
storage-locker.exampleUsage: Emergency equipment was kept in a labeled storage locker.

shower.definition: A place or device that sprays water over you so you can wash your body.
shower.exampleUsage: The crew member washed in the shower after the shift.

laundry.definition: The area or process for washing the crew’s clothing in this context.

recreation-room.definition: A room in a house or apartment set aside for games, relaxation, and casual time with others.

captain-s-cabin.definition: The private room or sleeping area assigned to the captain of a vessel.
captain-s-cabin.exampleUsage: The captain's cabin is near the control area.

captain.definition: The person in command of the vessel in this context.

navigator.definition: The ship's officer in charge of navigation.

engineer.definition: A crew specialist responsible for engineering systems and machinery within the assigned role.
engineer.exampleUsage: The vessel’s engineer was responsible for the assigned machinery systems.

sonar-operator.definition: A crew member who monitors and interprets information from sonar equipment.
sonar-operator.exampleUsage: The sonar operator reported an underwater contact.

radio-operator.definition: A crew member responsible for operating radio communication equipment.
radio-operator.exampleUsage: The radio operator received a routine message.

cook.definition: A crew member responsible for preparing meals.

medic.definition: A crew member trained to provide medical assistance within the assigned qualifications.

technician.definition: A worker with practical expertise in maintaining, testing, or operating assigned technical equipment.

first-officer.definition: A senior officer who is usually second in command after the captain.
first-officer.exampleUsage: The first officer reviewed the navigation plan.

depth-meter.definition: An instrument or display used to measure and show depth below the water surface.
depth-meter.exampleUsage: The depth meter updated as the vessel descended.

sea-chart.definition: A map specially designed for navigation at sea, showing coastlines, depths, hazards, and other marine information.
sea-chart.exampleUsage: The crew compared the electronic route with the sea chart.

gps.definition: A navigational system involving satellites and computers that can determine the latitude and longitude of a receiver on Earth by computing the time difference for signals from different satellites to reach the receiver.

buoy.definition: A float attached by rope to the seabed to mark channels in a harbor or underwater hazards.

anchor.definition: A heavy device lowered to help hold a vessel in place by gripping the bottom.

searchlight.definition: A light source with reflectors that projects a beam of light in a particular direction.

underwater-camera.definition: A camera designed or protected so it can take images while submerged in water.
underwater-camera.exampleUsage: The underwater camera recorded the seabed.

echo-sounder.definition: A device measures underwater distances by sending a sound pulse and timing its returning echo.
echo-sounder.exampleUsage: The echo sounder measured distance by timing returning sound.

current-meter.definition: An instrument that measures the speed, and sometimes direction, of moving water.
current-meter.exampleUsage: The current meter recorded the water flow outside the vessel.

logbook.definition: A book in which the log is written.

whale.definition: A very large marine mammal that breathes air through a blowhole.

shark.definition: A cartilaginous fish with gill slits, typically a streamlined body, and fins.

jellyfish.definition: An aquatic animal with a soft gelatinous body and tentacles, many species of which can sting.

giant-squid.definition: A very large deep-sea squid belonging to the genus Architeuthis.
giant-squid.exampleUsage: A museum display explained how giant squid live in deep ocean water.

anglerfish.definition: Fishes having large mouths with a wormlike filament attached for luring prey.
anglerfish.exampleUsage: The documentary showed an anglerfish with a lure near its mouth.

sea-turtle.definition: Large turtles that spend most of their lives in tropical or subtropical oceans come ashore mainly to lay eggs on sandy beaches.

coral.definition: A marine invertebrate that commonly forms colonies; many reef-building corals produce hard skeletons.

seaweed.definition: Plant growing in the sea, especially marine algae.

plankton.definition: Organisms that drift in water and generally cannot swim against the prevailing currents.
plankton.exampleUsage: The sample contained plankton drifting with the water.

shipwreck.definition: The remains of a ship that has sunk or been destroyed.

sonar.definition: Equipment that uses underwater sound to detect or investigate objects, either by listening or by transmitting and receiving echoes.
sonar.exampleUsage: The guide contrasted passive sonar listening with active sonar sending pulses.

radio.definition: A device for communication using radio waves.

engine.definition: A machine that converts energy into mechanical work for the vessel or its equipment.
engine.exampleUsage: The engineer inspected the engine that supplied mechanical power.

pump.definition: A machine that moves water or other fluid through a system.

valve.definition: Control consisting of a mechanical device for controlling the flow of a fluid.
valve.exampleUsage: The engineer identified the valve controlling fluid flow in the pipe.

officer.definition: Any person in the armed services who holds a position of authority or command.

bathroom.definition: A room containing facilities for washing, and often a toilet.

library.definition: A room or building containing books and other resources for reading, study, or reference.
